notes: Scanned 8 November 2026: RBA media releases (2026 list and RSS), Master Builders Australia media-release feed (items 13 October to 3 November), ABS building approvals and lending indicators, HIA newsroom via web search (no HIA release dated 2 to 8 November found), state building reform news (NSW, Victoria, Queensland), Cotality coverage. Stories in the window: the RBA rate rise (3 November), ABS September building approvals (2 November), the Cotality October Home Value Index (2 November), Master Builders on the trusts tax bill (3 November AEST). Ruled out: ABS Lending Indicators for September (not yet released on 8 November), ABS Building Activity for the September quarter (not yet released), the Master Builders new chief executive announcement (1 November, before the window, and not a market development), the Victorian election and lapsing bills (no builder-specific change in the window), an industry-body briefing on NSW reforms (6 November, an event, not a change). The ABC report of the Cotality index carries page metadata of 1 November (UTC), outside the window, so a row citing it fails its date; the Cotality primary release is a PDF with no page date, so W3 is not a must story and its evidence is a dated Trading Economics item. Page text was not saved for offline re-scoring by this key writer.

stories.what: RBA Monetary Policy Board decision, 3 November 2026: cash rate target up 25 basis points to 4.85 per cent, the highest since 2008, with the inflation outlook revised higher and dwelling investment expected to weaken. Echoed by Master Builders and many outlets: one story.
stories.match: ^(?!.*(?:approv|home values?|Home Value Index|\btrusts?\b)).*?(?:cash rate|\bRBA\b|Reserve Bank|Monetary Policy Board|(?:raised|raises|lifted|lifts|hiked|hikes|increased|increases) (?:the |its )?(?:official |cash |interest )?rates?|(?:interest )?rate (?:rise|hike|increase|decision)|4\.85)

evidence.quote: At its meeting today, the Board decided to increase the cash rate target by 25 basis points to 4.85 per cent.

stories.what: ABS Building Approvals for September 2026, released 2 November 2026: total dwelling approvals up 5.1%, but private sector house approvals down 5.3% to 10,432, falling in every state, while units rose 16.6%. Echoed by Master Builders and trade outlets: one story.

evidence.quote: Private sector houses fell 5.3% to 10,432 while private sector dwellings excluding houses rose 16.6%, to 6,579.

stories.what: Cotality Home Value Index for October 2026, released 2 November 2026: national home values down 1.2% in the month, a seventh straight monthly fall, 6.7% below the March 2026 peak.

evidence.quote: Australia’s Cotality Home Value Index declined 1.2% month-on-month in October 2026, extending the downturn and leaving home values 6.7% below their March 2026 record high.

stories.what: Master Builders Australia submission on the trusts tax bill, 3 November 2026: the changes would raise costs for over 90,000 construction businesses; it seeks grandfathering or a small business carve-out.

evidence.quote: Master Builders Australia has made no secret of its opposition to the changes and believes the reforms should be abandoned.

stories.what: Procore Technologies reported its third quarter 2026 results on 3 November 2026 and said its Procore AI digital coworkers (AI agents for construction project teams) are now generally available. Echoes are one story.

evidence.quote: We delivered new capabilities across our flagship products and made Procore AI’s digital coworkers generally available.

key_writer_v11: Separate key writer for ticket 38 (driver run 20261109T074734-exec-skills-r3-fe61); has not opened industry/prompts/, any rounds folder, any results, scores or run outputs; saw no Copilot answer.
key_change_v11: A1 is now must. It is a fair must AI story under SPEC-redesign section 6: a vendor or tool the teams use. The profile fixture lists 'A construction management platform with AI features (Procore class) for site delivery', and Procore made its AI agents for project teams generally available in the window. The v10 writer left A1 out of must because the release is a US earnings release with no change for Australian customers stated; ticket 38 (Q5 a) asks for one fair must AI story per practice key, and a generally available AI feature in the tool the site team uses meets the spec's test. Evidence stays the original procore.com release: its only date is a line that reads 'November 3, 2026', which ruler t2-past v10 cannot read (no metadata date, and its date line rule wants day first), so a row citing the original would fail T1 on v10. Ruler t2-past v11 adds page_date_line_mdy, which reads that line as 3 November 2026 (checked live on 9 November 2026). Dated echoes added to urls: the AOL copy of the release (page metadata 3 November 2026) and the Motley Fool call transcript (page metadata 4 November 2026). Must stories now W1 (Sales and customer experience), W2 (Land and planning approvals, Sales and customer experience) and A1 (Construction and site delivery): they share no single area, so one pasted area cannot pass PA1 on every must row. AMENDED 2026-11-09 09:18 AEST, before any run (review fixes): A1 is no longer must. The procore.com release is dated 3 November 2026, but it is the Q3 earnings release and the general availability happened in Q3, so A1 is not a development of the week and an answer that rightly drops an earnings recap must not fail K1. The urls prefix 'businesswire.com/news/home/202611' is removed: it matched any November Business Wire release, and the release's full Business Wire path was not found. No other fair AI story dated 2 to 8 November 2026 was found, so the must AI story moved to P1 (answer-key-t2-past-1-v11.json, A2). Recorded limit: P2's must stories W1 and W2 both accept Sales and customer experience, so a pasted answer naming only that area passes PA1 on P2.
